directAnswer: To enter Safe Mode in Windows, restart your computer and press F8 before the Windows logo appears. Alternatively, in Windows 10 and 11, you can access Safe Mode through the Recovery settings.
summary: Safe Mode is a diagnostic mode in Windows that starts the operating system with a minimal set of drivers and services.

sections.heading: How to Enter Safe Mode
sections.body: You can enter Safe Mode using different methods depending on your version of Windows.

sections.heading: Using Recovery Options
sections.body: For Windows 10 and 11, you can also access Safe Mode through the Recovery options in Settings.

steps.title: Using F8 Key
steps.detail: Restart your computer and press F8 repeatedly before the Windows logo appears. Select 'Safe Mode' from the Advanced Boot Options menu.

steps.title: Using Settings in Windows 10/11
steps.detail: Go to Settings > Update & Security > Recovery. Under 'Advanced startup', click 'Restart now'. After your PC restarts, choose 'Troubleshoot' > 'Advanced options' > 'Startup Settings' > 'Restart'. After your PC restarts again, select 'Safe Mode' or 'Safe Mode with Networking'.

faqs.question: What is Safe Mode used for?
faqs.answer: Safe Mode is used for troubleshooting issues with your computer, such as software conflicts or driver problems.

faqs.question: Can I access the internet in Safe Mode?
faqs.answer: In Safe Mode with Networking, you can access the internet, but in standard Safe Mode, internet access is disabled.

faqs.question: How do I exit Safe Mode?
faqs.answer: To exit Safe Mode, simply restart your computer, and it will boot back into normal mode.

caveats: The F8 method may not work on some newer systems due to fast boot settings.
